records.statement: document_variants parsing: the option value is a ":"-separated variant list, each variant "name" or "name=tags" (see Document_Build in Pure). the doc sessions all use a single bare name, but parse properly: split on ":", take the part before "=" of each, map EVERY variant name to the session (harmless for singletons, correct for multi-variant sessions).

where the catalog struct lives: mcp_session.scala already owns the startup structure/deps; a small Doc_Catalog object in mcp/src (own file or inside mcp_session.scala) keeping {sections, entry -> source resolution} — decide when writing, doc_read consumes the same object (its plan assumes it).

Doc.contents needs ML_Settings (the examples section expands $ML_SOURCES): ML_Settings.init() at startup, once. if init proves awkward in the server context, degrade to release_notes() ++ main_contents() and drop examples — pin which in the implementation notes.

heading extraction mechanism. two candidates: (a) line-anchored scan: a heading command at the start of a line (^chapter/^section/... followed by whitespace or an opening delimiter) with the title read from the following cartouche ‹...› or quoted string. the doc sources are hand-formatted prose theories; headings there are line-initial in practice. (b) token-based: outer-syntax token stream (isabelle.Token / Thy_Header + the session base's overall_syntax from deps), taking command tokens named chapter/section/... — immune to formatting, and the same machinery the plans/session_structure filesystem-/commands spike needs. decision rule: if that spike has landed its scala-side outer-syntax spans by the time this is implemented, REUSE it (b); otherwise ship (a) with the line-initial caveat pinned in a test (T6 guards against silent breakage across distribution upgrades). do not build (b) from scratch just for this tool.

heading commands with markers/attributes (chapter \<open>..\<close>, section \<^marker>...): the doc sources use plain forms today; (a) must at least skip an optional target/marker before the title or tolerate extraction failure per-heading (drop the row, never crash the toc).

cap sizes (revised 2026-07-14 during implementation): there was nothing to reuse — no ?lines= parser and no window constant exist anywhere in the codebase yet (isabelle://theory/{name} reads the whole file via start=0/stop=-1). doc_read is the FIRST tool to implement the spec's oversized-read rule, so it establishes Doc_Catalog.window_lines = 200 as the cap, applied to manual section reads and parameterless plain-entry reads alike; a chapter-sized section is EXPECTED to truncate — the note says how to narrow (a more specific section, or an explicit lines= for plain entries).
